about: WEKA learners described as data: options (WEKA's property names, flags, defaults, ranges and help) and the command line in the order WEKA prints it (getOptions). Read by the frontend (lib/learnerOptions.ts) and the backend (R/ml.R, a copy kept identical by a test). cmd items: {opt} an option, {lit} fixed tokens, {tpl} a flag whose argument is built from options, {sep} WEKA's '--' before the options of the next part; 'if' lists conditions that must all hold.

zeror.name: ZeroR
zeror.description: Baseline: always predicts the most common class (or the mean). A useful model must beat it.
zeror.about: Predicts the most frequent class for a class target and the mean for a numeric target, ignoring every attribute. Its scores are the baseline that any useful model has to beat.
zeror.reference: Witten, I. H., Frank, E., Hall, M. A., & Pal, C. J. (2016). Data mining: Practical machine learning tools and techniques (4th ed.). Morgan Kaufmann.

oner.name: OneR
oner.description: One rule on the single best attribute: a simple, readable baseline. Classes only.
oner.about: Builds one rule for each attribute (numeric attributes are cut into buckets) and keeps the attribute whose rule makes the fewest errors on the training data.
oner.reference: Holte, R. C. (1993). Very simple classification rules perform well on most commonly used datasets. Machine Learning, 11, 63–91.

options.name: minBucketSize
options.label: Minimum cases per bucket
options.help: Numeric attributes are cut into buckets with at least this many cases of the majority class.

jrip.name: JRip
jrip.description: RIPPER: a short list of if-then rules, grown and pruned class by class. Classes only.
jrip.about: Repeated incremental pruning to produce error reduction (RIPPER): rules are grown for each class in turn, pruned on a held-back part of the training data and then optimised.
jrip.reference: Cohen, W. W. (1995). Fast effective rule induction. Proceedings of the 12th International Conference on Machine Learning, 115–123.

options.name: usePruning
options.label: Pruning
options.help: Prune the rules on a held-back part of the training data.

options.name: folds
options.label: Folds for pruning
options.help: The training data are split into this many folds; one fold is used for pruning.

options.name: checkErrorRate
options.label: Stop when the error rate reaches 50%
options.help: Stop adding rules once a rule's error rate is 50% or more.

options.name: minNo
options.label: Minimum weight of cases per rule
options.help: Each rule must cover at least this total weight of cases.

options.name: optimizations
options.label: Optimisation runs
options.help: Number of times the rule set is optimised after it is grown.

options.name: seed
options.label: Seed
options.help: Seed for shuffling the data before they are split for pruning.

part.name: PART
part.description: A decision list made from partial C4.5 trees: readable rules. Classes only.
part.about: Builds a partial C4.5 decision tree in each step and turns its best leaf into a rule, giving an ordered list of rules (a decision list).
part.reference: Frank, E., & Witten, I. H. (1998). Generating accurate rule sets without global optimization. Proceedings of the 15th International Conference on Machine Learning, 144–151.

options.name: unpruned
options.label: Unpruned rules
options.help: Do not prune the partial trees the rules come from.

options.name: confidenceFactor
options.label: Confidence factor
options.help: Confidence factor for error-based pruning: smaller values prune more.

off.msg: Not used: the rules are unpruned.

options.name: reducedErrorPruning
options.label: Reduced-error pruning
options.help: Prune on a held-out fold of the training data instead of the confidence estimate.

off.msg: Not used: the rules are unpruned.

options.name: numFolds
options.label: Folds for reduced-error pruning
options.help: The training data are split into this many folds; one fold is used for pruning.

options.name: seed
options.label: Seed for the pruning folds
options.help: Seed for shuffling the data before they are split into the pruning folds.

options.name: minNumObj
options.label: Minimum cases per rule
options.help: Each rule must cover at least this many cases.

options.name: binarySplits
options.label: Binary splits
options.help: Split nominal attributes into two groups of labels instead of one branch per label.

options.name: useMDLcorrection
options.label: MDL correction
options.help: Correct the information gain of numeric split points by the minimum description length principle.

options.name: doNotMakeSplitPointActualValue
options.label: Split points between values
options.help: Faster: numeric split points stay midway between values instead of being moved to an actual value in the data.

dtable.name: DecisionTable
dtable.description: A lookup table on the best subset of attributes, chosen by best-first search.
dtable.about: Chooses a small subset of attributes by best-first search, scored by cross-validation, and predicts from a table of the training cases on those attributes (the majority class or the mean of the matching cases).
dtable.reference: Kohavi, R. (1995). The power of decision tables. Proceedings of the 8th European Conference on Machine Learning, 174–189.

options.name: crossVal
options.label: Folds to score subsets (1 = leave-one-out)
options.help: Cross-validation used to score each subset of attributes; 1 is leave-one-out.

options.name: evaluationMeasure
options.label: Score subsets by
options.help: The measure the attribute search tries to improve.

options.name: search (BestFirst -D)
options.label: Search direction
options.help: Direction of the best-first search through the subsets of attributes.

options.name: search (BestFirst -N)
options.label: Stop after non-improving subsets
options.help: The search stops after this many expansions that do not improve the score.

options.name: useIBk
options.label: Nearest neighbour for unmatched cases
options.help: A case with no matching table entry is predicted from its nearest neighbour instead of the overall majority (or mean).

stump.name: DecisionStump
stump.description: A tree with a single split: a quick baseline and a common base learner for boosting.
stump.about: A one-level decision tree: a single split on the best attribute, with a separate branch for missing values.
stump.reference: Iba, W., & Langley, P. (1992). Induction of one-level decision trees. Proceedings of the 9th International Workshop on Machine Learning, 233–240.

reptree.name: REPTree
reptree.description: A fast tree grown on information gain (or variance) and pruned on held-back data.
reptree.about: A fast decision or regression tree: splits by information gain (variance for a numeric target), then reduced-error pruning on a held-back fold. Numeric attributes are sorted only once.
reptree.reference: Witten, I. H., Frank, E., Hall, M. A., & Pal, C. J. (2016). Data mining: Practical machine learning tools and techniques (4th ed.). Morgan Kaufmann.

options.name: minNum
options.label: Minimum cases per leaf
options.help: A leaf must hold at least this many cases (in total weight).

options.name: maxDepth
options.label: Maximum depth (−1 = no limit)
options.help: Maximum depth of the tree; −1 sets no limit.

options.name: minVarianceProp
options.label: Minimum variance share for a split
options.help: A node is split only when its variance is at least this share of the variance of all training cases.

options.name: noPruning
options.label: No pruning
options.help: Keep the full tree.

options.name: numFolds
options.label: Folds for pruning
options.help: The training data are split into this many folds; one fold is used for pruning.

off.msg: Not used: the tree is not pruned.

options.name: seed
options.label: Seed
options.help: Seed for shuffling the data before they are split into the pruning folds.

off.msg: Not used: the tree is not pruned.

options.name: initialCount
options.label: Initial class count
options.help: Added to the class counts of every leaf (smooths the leaf probabilities).

options.name: spreadInitialCount
options.label: Spread the initial count over the classes
options.help: Divide the initial count over the classes instead of adding it to each class.

rtree.name: RandomTree
rtree.description: One unpruned tree that tries a random few attributes at each split.
rtree.about: Grows an unpruned tree that considers only a random subset of the attributes at each node. One RandomTree is the building block of WEKA's random forest.
rtree.reference: Breiman, L. (2001). Random forests. Machine Learning, 45, 5–32.

options.name: KValue
options.label: Attributes tried per split (0 = automatic)
options.help: Number of attributes drawn at random at each node; 0 uses log₂(attributes) + 1.

options.name: seed
options.label: Seed
options.help: Seed for drawing the attributes.

options.name: breakTiesRandomly
options.label: Break ties at random
options.help: When several attributes are equally good, pick one at random.

options.name: minNum
options.label: Minimum cases per leaf
options.help: A leaf must hold at least this total weight of cases.

options.name: maxDepth
options.label: Maximum depth (0 = no limit)
options.help: Maximum depth of the tree; 0 sets no limit.

options.name: minVarianceProp
options.label: Minimum variance share for a split
options.help: A node is split only when its variance is at least this share of the variance of all training cases.

options.name: numFolds
options.label: Folds for backfitting (0 = none)
options.help: Grow the tree on part of the data and fit the leaf estimates on the rest; 0 does no backfitting.

options.name: allowUnclassifiedInstances
options.label: Allow unclassified cases
options.help: Leave a case unclassified when it reaches an empty leaf, instead of using the parent's estimate.

wrf.name: RandomForest
wrf.description: WEKA's random forest: many RandomTrees on bootstrap samples, voting together.
wrf.about: Breiman's random forest as WEKA builds it: bagging of RandomTrees, each grown on a bootstrap sample and trying a random subset of attributes at each split.
wrf.reference: Breiman, L. (2001). Random forests. Machine Learning, 45, 5–32.

options.name: numIterations
options.label: Trees
options.help: Number of trees in the forest.

options.name: bagSizePercent
options.label: Bag size (% of the training data)
options.help: Size of each bootstrap sample as a percentage of the training data.

options.name: calcOutOfBag
options.label: Out-of-bag error
options.help: Estimate the error from the cases left out of each bag; shown in the classifier model.

options.name: seed
options.label: Seed
options.help: Seed for the bootstrap samples and the attributes drawn.

options.name: numFeatures
options.label: Attributes tried per split (0 = automatic)
options.help: Number of attributes drawn at random at each node; 0 uses log₂(attributes) + 1.

options.name: maxDepth
options.label: Maximum depth (0 = no limit)
options.help: Maximum depth of each tree; 0 sets no limit.

options.name: minNum
options.label: Minimum cases per leaf
options.help: A leaf must hold at least this total weight of cases.

options.name: minVarianceProp
options.label: Minimum variance share for a split
options.help: A node is split only when its variance is at least this share of the variance of all training cases.

options.name: breakTiesRandomly
options.label: Break ties at random
options.help: When several attributes are equally good, pick one at random.

m5p.name: M5P
m5p.description: A model tree: a tree whose leaves hold linear regressions. Numeric targets only.
m5p.about: Quinlan's M5 model tree, as improved by Wang and Witten: a regression tree whose leaves hold linear models, pruned. Predictions are not smoothed (-U): the WEKA version that R runs (3.9.3) gives wrong smoothed predictions, so PathLab uses the leaf models as they are.
m5p.reference: Quinlan, J. R. (1992). Learning with continuous classes. Proceedings of the 5th Australian Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence, 343–348. Wang, Y., & Witten, I. H. (1997). Induction of model trees for predicting continuous classes. Poster papers of the 9th European Conference on Machine Learning.

options.name: minNumInstances
options.label: Minimum cases per leaf
options.help: A leaf must hold at least this many cases.

options.name: unpruned
options.label: Unpruned tree
options.help: Keep the full tree.

options.name: buildRegressionTree
options.label: Regression tree (constant leaves)
options.help: Predict a constant in each leaf instead of a linear model.

lmt.name: LMT
lmt.description: A logistic model tree: a tree with logistic regressions in its leaves. Classes only.
lmt.about: Logistic model trees: a decision tree whose leaves hold logistic regression models, fitted by LogitBoost with the number of iterations chosen by cross-validation.
lmt.reference: Landwehr, N., Hall, M., & Frank, E. (2005). Logistic model trees. Machine Learning, 59, 161–205.

options.name: minNumInstances
options.label: Minimum cases to split a node
options.help: A node is split only when it holds at least this many cases.

options.name: convertNominal
options.label: Binary splits
options.help: Turn nominal attributes into binary ones before growing the tree.

options.name: splitOnResiduals
options.label: Split on residuals
options.help: Choose splits on the residuals of the logistic models instead of the class values.

options.name: doNotMakeSplitPointActualValue
options.label: Split points between values
options.help: Faster: numeric split points stay midway between values instead of being moved to an actual value in the data.

options.name: numBoostingIterations
options.label: LogitBoost iterations (−1 = by cross-validation)
options.help: A fixed number of LogitBoost iterations; −1 chooses it by cross-validation.

options.name: fastRegression
options.label: Fast heuristic for the iterations
options.help: Choose the number of iterations once, at the root, instead of by cross-validation at every node (much faster).

options.name: errorOnProbabilities
options.label: Stop on the error of the probabilities
options.help: Choose the iterations by the error of the probabilities (RMSE) instead of the misclassification error.

options.name: useAIC
options.label: Choose the iterations by AIC
options.help: Use the Akaike information criterion instead of cross-validation to choose the iterations.

options.name: weightTrimBeta
options.label: Weight trimming β (0 = none)
options.help: Share of the weight mass LogitBoost may ignore to speed up; 0 trims nothing.

logistic.name: Logistic
logistic.description: WEKA's multinomial logistic regression with a small ridge penalty. Classes only.
logistic.about: Multinomial logistic regression with a ridge estimator (le Cessie & van Houwelingen), fitted by quasi-Newton optimisation. WEKA replaces missing values and turns nominal attributes into binary ones.
logistic.reference: le Cessie, S., & van Houwelingen, J. C. (1992). Ridge estimators in logistic regression. Applied Statistics, 41, 191–201.

options.name: ridge
options.label: Ridge
options.help: Penalty on the size of the coefficients: larger values shrink them more.

options.name: maxIts
options.label: Maximum iterations (−1 = until convergence)
options.help: Upper limit on the optimisation steps; −1 runs until convergence.

options.name: useConjugateGradientDescent
options.label: Conjugate gradient descent
options.help: Optimise by conjugate gradient descent instead of BFGS updates; faster with many attributes.

slogistic.name: SimpleLogistic
slogistic.description: Logistic regression built by LogitBoost, which selects attributes as it goes. Classes only.
slogistic.about: Linear logistic regression models fitted by LogitBoost with simple regression functions as base learners; the number of iterations is chosen by cross-validation, which also selects the attributes.
slogistic.reference: Landwehr, N., Hall, M., & Frank, E. (2005). Logistic model trees. Machine Learning, 59, 161–205. Sumner, M., Frank, E., & Hall, M. (2005). Speeding up logistic model tree induction. PKDD 2005, 675–683.

options.name: numBoostingIterations
options.label: Fixed iterations (0 = by cross-validation)
options.help: A fixed number of LogitBoost iterations; 0 chooses it automatically.

options.name: maxBoostingIterations
options.label: Maximum iterations
options.help: Upper limit on the iterations when they are chosen automatically.

options.name: heuristicStop
options.label: Early-stopping heuristic (0 = off)
options.help: Stop when the error has not improved for this many iterations; 0 turns the heuristic off.

options.name: useCrossValidation
options.label: Choose the iterations by cross-validation
options.help: Off: choose them by the error on the training data instead (faster, but may overfit).

options.name: errorOnProbabilities
options.label: Stop on the error of the probabilities
options.help: Use the error of the probabilities (RMSE) instead of the misclassification error.

options.name: useAIC
options.label: Choose the iterations by AIC
options.help: Use the Akaike information criterion instead of cross-validation.

options.name: weightTrimBeta
options.label: Weight trimming β (0 = none)
options.help: Share of the weight mass LogitBoost may ignore to speed up; 0 trims nothing.

bayesnet.name: BayesNet
bayesnet.description: A Bayesian network learned from the data; relaxes Naive Bayes' independence. Classes only.
bayesnet.about: Learns the structure of a Bayesian network over the attributes and the class with a search algorithm and a score, then estimates its conditional probability tables. WEKA discretises numeric attributes.
bayesnet.reference: Bouckaert, R. R. (2004). Bayesian network classifiers in WEKA (Working Paper 14/2004). University of Waikato.

options.name: searchAlgorithm
options.label: Search algorithm

choices.label: K2 (hill climbing in a fixed order)

options.help: How the network structure is searched for.

options.name: maxNrOfParents
options.label: Maximum parents per node
options.help: Each attribute may depend on at most this many other nodes besides the class; 1 gives Naive Bayes plus at most one link.

off.msg: TAN uses one parent per attribute.

options.name: scoreType
options.label: Score
options.help: The score that compares candidate structures.

options.name: estimator alpha
options.label: Initial count (α)
options.help: Added to every count when the probability tables are estimated, so no probability is zero.

adaboost.name: AdaBoostM1
adaboost.description: Boosting: weak learners trained in turn, each focusing on the cases the last ones got wrong. Classes only.
adaboost.about: Freund and Schapire's AdaBoost.M1: each round reweights the training cases so the next base learner concentrates on the misclassified ones; the rounds vote, weighted by their accuracy.
adaboost.reference: Freund, Y., & Schapire, R. E. (1996). Experiments with a new boosting algorithm. Proceedings of the 13th International Conference on Machine Learning, 148–156.

options.name: numIterations
options.label: Iterations
options.help: Number of boosting rounds (base learners).

options.name: weightThreshold
options.label: Weight mass used (%)
options.help: Train each round on the cases holding this share of the weight; lower values (around 90) speed it up.

options.name: useResampling
options.label: Resample instead of reweighting
options.help: Draw a weighted sample for each round instead of passing the weights to the base learner.

options.name: seed
options.label: Seed
options.help: Seed for resampling.

options.name: classifier
options.label: Base learner
options.help: The learner boosted in each round, with WEKA's default options.

bagging.name: Bagging
bagging.description: Bagging: the same learner trained on many bootstrap samples, then averaged.
bagging.about: Breiman's bootstrap aggregating: the base learner is trained on many bootstrap samples of the training data and their predictions are averaged (or voted), which reduces variance.
bagging.reference: Breiman, L. (1996). Bagging predictors. Machine Learning, 24, 123–140.

options.name: numIterations
options.label: Iterations (bags)
options.help: Number of bootstrap samples, each with its own base learner.

options.name: bagSizePercent
options.label: Bag size (% of the training data)
options.help: Size of each bootstrap sample as a percentage of the training data.

options.name: calcOutOfBag
options.label: Out-of-bag error
options.help: Estimate the error from the cases left out of each bag; shown in the classifier model.

options.name: seed
options.label: Seed
options.help: Seed for the bootstrap samples.

options.name: classifier
options.label: Base learner
options.help: The learner trained on each bootstrap sample, with WEKA's default options.
